2l. In the case of Municipal Committee, Bahadurgarh v. Krishnan Behari and others, (996) 2 LLN 
88l, wherein it was observed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court that act of misappropriation is relevant and 
the amount of misappropriation may be small or large. 


22. On perusal of case law in State Bank of India v. Ram Lal Bhaskar & Anr (202) | LLN 56, it 
appears that the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that there must be some evidence which may reasonably 
support the conclusion that delinquent employee is guilty of charge. __In the present case, the Petitioner 
has not pressed or challenged the validity of domestic enquiry and pleaded only to interfere with the 
quantum of punishment imposed by the Respondent Bank i.e, order of dismissal from service by 
exercising the power of this Tribunal u/s.llA of the Industrial Disputes Act, 947. 


23. In the case of UOI & Others Vs. Boshamber Das Dogra (MANU/SC/0887/2009) the employee 
remained absent without seeking permission or leave, he was punished for so many times and finally, he 
was removed from service. This order was upheld by the Hon'ble Supreme Court. The above case law is 
squarely applicable to the facts of the present case on hand, as the Petitioner in the present case remained 
absent unauthorizedly and according to the Respondent, the Petitioner is a chronic absentee. 


24. In the case of Ramana Vs. APSRT Corporation & Others (2005) गा LLJ 725, the Hon'ble 
Supreme Court held that the court should not interfere with the administrator’s decision unless it was 
illogical and suffers from procedural impropriety or was shocking the conscience of the court. 
Therefore, I find no reason to interfere with the impugned order passed by the Respondent Bank by 
exercising the powers of this Tribunal u/s.llA of the Industrial Disputes Act, 947 as both the charges 
levelled against the Petitioner were proved by the Respondent Bank.

Soon after the death, the wife of the deceased employee submitted an application before the management 
of ECL on 29.08.2004, claiming monetary compensation for herself as per provisions of NCWA and to 
keep the name of Brijesh Yadav in the Live Roster for his employment when he attained eighteen (8) 
years (Exhibit W-5). The application was considered and the management held screening of Usha Devi, the 
wife of the deceased on 7.09.2004. The Screening Report (Exhibit W-7) reveals that the age of Brijesh 
Yadav was four (4) years as on 4.07.995 and a daughter S. Kumari was one (() year old. In their report 
signed by the officials of the management it appears that they recommended Brijesh Yadav’s name to be 
maintained in the Live Roster of the colliery so that he gets employment after attaining majority. In letter 
No. 7?(/॥५७/(:-6/2004/ 253 dated 26/28.0.2004 (Exhibit W-8) issued by the Sr. P.O, Porascole Colliery

addressed to the Agent, Porascole Colliery it was proposed that the name of Brijesh Yadav may be kept in 
the Live Roster, maintained in the Colliery level as per rules vide letter No. ECL/DP/47/5995 dated 
9..999. For a considerable period, the management did not take any decision on the claim made by the 
dependents. A Pre-Employment Medical Examination of Brijesh Yadav was held on 28.04.2006 at Kajora 
Area and in the Report produced by the management as Exhibit M-3, the age of the minor son was 
recorded as thirteen and half (3’%2) years in Column No. (5). In column No. (6) the age was recorded as 
0 to 3 years on the basis of his appearance without holding any scientific test or examination for 
assessment of the age. On the basis of such report management conveniently remained silent without 
maintaining the name of Brijesh Yadav in the Live Roster, on the pretext that he was below twelve (2) 
years of age on the date of death of his father. In Exhibit M-4, a letter dated 23.09.205 issued by the Sr. 
Manager (P) Empl/ED addressed to the Chief Manager (2), Kajora Area, it was stated that the Competent 
Authority has considered the payment of MMCC to the widow of the deceased employee and had observed 
that the widow could apply for it with immediate effect by giving her Bank Account and other KYC 
details. The letter was silent regarding the claim for employment of the son. In June, 20l0 Usha Devi 
issued a reminder, informing that after screening was held for providing employment of her son Brijesh 
Yadav and monetary compensation to her but the management has not responded to the claims (Exhibit W- 
9). The widow submitted another application dated 22.03.202 (Exhibit W-l0) wherein she stated that at 
the time of death of her husband her son was thirteen (3) years of age and he has already attained 2] years 
of age and he is eligible for employment against the death of his father. In Form PS-3 the name of her son 
is mentioned against Serial No. 7. On perusing Form PS-3 (Exhibit ४४-6) I find that date of birth of 
Brijesh Yadav was recorded as 4.07.990. The entries were made on 25.05.998 which is much earlier to 
the date of death of the employee. In this matter it may be gathered from Exhibit W-2, a letter dated 
.03.20I5 issued by the Manager (P), Kajora Area addressed to the Sr. Manager(P) Empl/ED, ECL, 
Headquarters, that as per records available, the ex-employee has filled up PS-3 Form during his lifetime 
wherein the name of Brijesh Yadav is mentioned as son with date of birth recorded as 4.07.990, as such 
the age of Brijesh Yadav on the date of death of his father should have been computed as 3 years 0 
months and 27 days even though his date of birth was recorded as 05.0.99] in the Madhyamik 


Examination. 


4. For the purpose of considering the age of the dependent son on the date of death of his father, the 
management is duty bound to look into contemporaneous documents and other materials which existed 
prior to the death of the employee and which were acted upon by the management. It is true that the union 
has produced a Brith Certificate of the dependent son as Exhibit ४४-4, which bears his date of birth as 
05.0.99l. The said document was issued on 40.07.2003, before the death of the employee. In other 
documents, like the Admit Card of Madhyamik Siksha Parishad Uttar Pradesh Allahabad (Exhibit ४४-।5) 
the date of birth of Brijesh Yadav is recorded as 05.0.99l. The said document was based upon the date 
of birth recorded in the Brith Certificate and shall prevail over all other documents. Be that as it may the 
management of the employer company is bound by the age of the dependent son mentioned in the PS-3 
Form and by virtue of such date of birth the age of Brijesh Yadav should be considered as 43 years 40 
months and 27 days on the date of death of his father which is above the minimum age making him eligible 


for maintaining his name in the Live Roster.

5. In this case the Competent Authority of ECL has already approved the claim for monetary 
compensation to the widow of the deceased. According to the provisions of Clause 9.5.0 (ii) of NCWA-VII 
a female dependent has the right to exercise the option between employment and monetary compensation. 
The right vested in her can be taken away only by a process approved by the law. The management of the 
employer company therefore has no right to make the choice for the dependents of the deceased nor can it 
impose any conditions upon the dependents that monetary compensation would only be granted in lieu of 
employment. In clause 9.5.0 (iii) of NCWA-VII, during the period the male dependent is on the Live 
Roster, the female dependent will be paid monetary compensation as per rates at paragraphs (i) and (ii) 


above and this provision is made effective from 0.0.2000. 


6. It is to be borne in mind that the NCWA is a negotiated agreement that has been arrived at between 
the employer and the employees. It is a settlement under section 2 (p) of the Industrial Disputes Act, 947 
and has a binding effect on the parties thereto under section 8 (3) of the Industrial Disputes Act, 947. 
NCWA has made provisions for compassionate appointment for the dependents of the deceased employee. 
The claim for compassionate appointment is governed by the terms of employment of the deceased 
employee. None of the Clauses 9.3.0 to 9.5.0 of NCWA provide any time limit for applying or prescribe 
any financial solvency of the family as a disqualification. It does not allow the employer to choose between 
the dependents as to who it would grant the employment or the MMCC. In the present case the 
management has acted in an illegal and arbitrary manner by not taking the right course of action agreed 
upon by the employer and the employees in the NCWA. I find from the evidence on record that Usha Devi 
consistently prayed for maintaining the name of her son in the Live Roster, as he was above twelve (2) 
years of age on the date of death of his father and for providing employment to him on his attaining 
majority. She also prayed for payment of monetary compensation to her from the date of death of her 
husband till employment was granted to her son which is permissible under Cluse 9.5.0 (iii) of NCWA-VII. 
The management by treating Brijesh Yadav below twelve (2) years on the date of death of his father has 
acted in an illegal manner to deprive the dependent son from employment as per NCWA. The evidence on 
record clearly reveals that at the time the son was over thirteen (3) years of age but only to deprive him, 
management acted in an unfair way and recorded the age of the candidate as l0 to 3 years by his 
appearance only, without considering PS-3 Form and Birth Registration Certificate of the dependent son 


during the medical examination. 


7. I therefore find and hold that Brijesh Yadav was above twelve (2) years of age on the date of 
death of his father i.e., .06.2004 and now a major is entitled to get employment on compassionate ground 
as per provisions of NCWA. Usha Devi, the wife of the deceased employee is also entitled to monetary 
compensation from the date of death of employee i.e., .06.2004 till employment is provided to Brijesh 
Yadav under the management of ECL. The act of management in not providing employment by not 
maintaining the name of the minor son in the Live Roster at the appropriate time and not providing 
monetary compensation to the widow is not tenable under the law and rules applicable. The management of 
Porascole Colliery under Kajora Area of ECL is therefore directed to provide employment to Brijesh 
Yadav, son of Late Narendra Yadav after completing all formalities within two (2) months from the date of 
communication of the Award. The management shall also pay monetary compensation to Usha Devi at the 
applicable rate from .06.2004 till Brijesh Yadav is provided with employment. The Industrial Dispute is 


accordingly decided in favour of the union.
